'''''Star Wars: Andor''''', titled on-screen as '''''Andor''''' and later marketed as '''''Andor: A Star Wars Story''''' for the second season, is an American [[Wikipedia:Live-action|live-action]] [[Wikipedia:Television_show|television series]] developed by [[Lucasfilm]] and released on [[Disney+]]. The series is a [[spy]] thriller starring [[Diego Luna]], reprising his role as [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]] from the [[2016]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. The [[Andor Season 1|first season]] premiered in [[September]] [[2022]], and the [[Andor Season 2|second season]] premiered on [[April 22]], [[2025]] with a new logo.

==Official description==
''The ''Andor'' series will explore a new perspective from the ''Star Wars'' galaxy, focusing on Cassian Andor's journey to discover the difference he can make. The series brings forward the tale of the burgeoning rebellion against the Empire and how people and planets became involved. It's an era filled with danger, deception and intrigue where Cassian will embark on the path that is destined to turn him into a rebel hero.<ref name="Media kit" />''

==Development==
====Announcement====
{{Quote|Going back to the ''Star Wars'' universe is very special for me. I have so many memories of the great work we did together and the relationships I made throughout the journey. We have a fantastic adventure ahead of us, and this new exciting format will give us the chance to explore this character more deeply.|Diego Luna, on reprising his role|<ref name="Announcement" />}}
Talks for a television series focused on [[Cassian Jeron Andor]], [[Diego Luna]]'s character from the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', began before the Anthology film was released, though Luna had doubts that it would happen.<ref name="IMDb">{{IMDb|url=video/vi1766702873?listId=ls025849840|text=Diego Luna Knows How to Play an Authentic Villain and Raise a Future Jedi|archivedate=20200424211503}}</ref> In [[February]] [[2018]], Disney CEO [[Bob Iger (chief executive officer)|Bob Iger]] revealed that "a few" ''Star Wars'' live-action series were in development for [[Disney+|Disney's streaming service]].<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/star-wars-tv-series-disney-developing-a-few-streaming-service-1082523|text='Star Wars' TV Series: Disney Developing "a Few" for Its Streaming Service|author=Lesley Goldberg, Aaron Couch|date=2018-02-06|archivedate=20200307153245}}</ref> The series was officially announced by Iger during a Disney quarterly earnings call on [[November 8]], 2018.<ref name="Announcement" />

Series (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Jacob Fisher|date=2019-07-11|work=[https://discussingfilm.net DiscussingFilm]|archivedate=20200407112233}}</ref> On October 15, 2019, Variety reported that ''Rogue One'' Series at Disney Plus (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Joe Otterson|date=2019-10-15|archivedate=20200403065859}}</ref>

Lucasfilm's original concept for the series focused on the adventures of Andor and his reprogrammed [[KX-series security droid]], [[K-2SO]], who is played by [[Alan Tudyk]]. The two would have a [[Wikipedia:Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid|Butch and Sundance]] style dynamic, with the two set to storm a citadel<ref name="Real People">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How ‘Andor' Became the First ‘Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: ‘I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|archivedate=20220824140042}}</ref> in the series pilot.<ref name="Controversial Story">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1857713/andor-showrunner-tony-gilroy-most-controversial-storyline-explained|text=Andor Showrunner Tony Gilroy Addresses The Series' Most Controversial Storyline [Exclusive Interview]|author=Pearson, Ben|archivedate=20250515031238}}</ref> Thanks to his work on ''Rogue One'', Gilroy was consulted for work on the prequel series.<ref name="TimesUnion">{{WebCite|url=https://www.timesunion.com/hudsonvalley/culture/article/tony-gilroy-andor-star-wars-profile-20326721.php|text=Tony Gilroy’s journey from the Hudson Valley to a galaxy far, far away|author=Gregory James Wakeman|work=''Times Union''|archivedate=20250519195229}}</ref> He thought the original pitch was "fine" but felt it was "very hard to sustain over a long haul,"<ref name="Real People" /> questioning what they could do after storming a citadel at the show's very start. Furthermore, he knew from his experience on ''Rogue One'' that K-2SO was a hard character to work with for long periods of time, which would make an entire series starring the character difficult, lest Lucasfilm wanted to have to find ways to hide him during many missions.<ref name="Controversial Story" />

[[File:Andor1-Cassiankillsguard.png|thumb|left|300px|Tony Gilroy's pitch for ''Andor'' took the character of Cassian Andor back five years and followed him into "the worst night of his life."]]
Without outright saying he was interested, Gilroy responded with what was later called "a long forensic manifesto" to Lucasfilm, outlining his issues with the pitch and putting forth his own ideas. Gilroy's idea was the story that would become ''Andor'',<ref name="Real People" /> pitching a story that took Andor himself "back five years, to the worst night of his life." In the process, the series would see Andor evolve into the man first seen in ''Rogue One''. According to Gilroy, Lucasfilm thought his pitch "looked a little insane,"<ref name="TimesUnion" /> and he fully admitted the story he had in mind was "a crazy idea" and "radical."<ref name="Real People" /> In the end, however, Lucasfilm decided Gilroy's story was the route to go.<ref name="TimesUnion" />

====Gilroy's concepts====
=====Overview=====
{{Expandsect}}
[[File:TonyGilroy-SWcom.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Tony Gilroy took inspiration from real-world history when writing ''Andor'']]
As far back as his pitch to Lucasfilm, Gilroy, as a student of history, wanted to imbue the series with themes of revolution, fascism, politics, rebellion, and the regular people caught up on those conflicts.<ref name="TimesUnion" /> When Gilroy was asked about political resonances in ''Andor'' in November 2022, he stated that the series was written without contemporary politics in mind, drawing on historical revolutions simply as spontaneous events to drive the characters' adventures—"whatever contemporary resonance it has is usually in the eye of the beholder. Oppression is oppression."<ref name="Oppression">{{WebCite|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/andor-not-political-disney-plus-tony-gilroy-interview-1234780620|text='Andor': Tony Gilroy's 'Star Wars' Series Wasn't Meant to be Political|author=Proma Khosla|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:IndieWire|''IndieWire'']]|archivedate=20230518200016}}</ref> In another November interview, Gilroy emphasized that his personal politics are "absolutely not important" to the series' themes and that ''Star Wars'' allows plentiful comparisons to history. As to the "age old question" of "who's a terrorist and who's a freedom fighter," Gilroy wanted every character to "speak for themselves" to make their motives believable and referred the idea of controversial revolutionaries to historical nation-building movements, naming the United States' [[Wikipedia:Thomas Jefferson|Thomas Jefferson]] and South Africa [[Wikipedia:Nelson Mandela|Nelson Mandela]] and further listing the revolutions of France, [[Wikipedia:Haiti|Haiti]], [[Wikipedia:October Revolution|Russia and the Soviet Union]], and the nation-building of Israel.<ref name="Themes">{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/article/andor-showrunner-tony-gilroy-interview-season-one-themes-hope-community-cassian-future|text=ANDOR Showrunner Tony Gilroy on Season 1's Powerful Themes and the Future|author=Michael Walsh|date=2022-11-23|archivedate=20221123110025}}</ref> The [[Rix Road (episode)|season one finale]] took inspiration from the 1966 [[Wikipedia:Gillo Pontecorvo|Gillo Pontecorvo]] film [[Wikipedia:The Battle of Algiers|''The Battle of Algiers'']], which was based on the [[Wikipedia:Algerian War|Algerian War of Independence]] against the colonial [[Wikipedia:French Fourth Republic|French government]].<ref name="Algiers">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/sharper-director-benjamin-caron-apple-movie-andor-1235356365|text=Sharper Director Benjamin Caron Talks Twisty Apple Movie, Andor|author=Brian Davids|date=2023-03-20|archivedate=20230320182210}}</ref>

Gilroy also likened ''Andor''{{'s}} character of [[Luthen Rael]] as a [[Wikipedia:Startup company|start-up company]] founder<ref name="Themes" /> and, earlier in September, identified the senator and eventual Rebel Alliance leader [[Mon Mothma]] as a "figurehead of [[Democracy|liberal democracy]] that will fail"<ref name="Mothma">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/09/mon-mothma-andor-star-wars|text=Who Is Mon Mothma? Star Wars Fans Are About To Be Shocked|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2022-09-27|archiveurl=https://archive.is/NZSCB}}</ref>—he compared her to [[Wikipedia:Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|US House Speaker]] [[Wikipedia:Nancy Pelosi|Nancy Pelosi]] in another interview in the same month.<ref name="Pelosi">{{WebCite|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/andor-syril-karn-mon-mothma-1234764813|text=Tony Gilroy Unpacks 'Andor' Ep. 4: Mon Mothma Is 'a Nancy Pelosi Character'|author=Proma Khosla|date=2022-09-28|work=[[Wikipedia:IndieWire|''IndieWire'']]|archivedate=20230507110140}}</ref> [[Fiona Shaw]], who played [[Maarva Carassi Andor|Maarva Andor]] and spoke in an interview released in August 2022, thought that Gilroy's story is a "scurrilous" and "[[Wikipedia:Social realism|social-realist]]" take on "the [[Wikipedia:Donald Trump|Trumpian]] world" that was "exploding in different places right now" with people's rights being taken away.<ref name="Trumpian world" />

=====Five season plan=====
{{Quote|We were halfway through shooting season 1, coming through Covid, and the monumental size of the show, the effort, and everything else was just dawning on us. We realized that I didn't have enough calories to do it, and Diego's face couldn't take the timing, because it just takes too long to make it. We were saved by Disney saying, 'Okay, if you guys can figure out a way to do it, we're into it.|Tony Gilroy, on shifting to two seasons|<ref name="Radar03-26-25">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/star-wars-tv-shows/andor-showrunner-says-season-2s-more-fast-paced-structure-is-a-fascinating-experiment-that-is-born-out-of-desperation-i-dont-know-if-anyones-ever-done-it-before|text=Andor showrunner says season 2's more fast-paced structure is a "fascinating experiment" that is "born out of desperation": "I don't know if anyone's ever done it before"|author=Russell, Bradley and Edwards, Richard|date=2025-03-26|archivedate=20250331024316}}</ref>}}
[[File:LegoAndor.png|thumb|left|200px|[[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] sets based on ''Andor'' have released]]
Originally, Gilroy thought of ''Andor'' as a five season show<ref name="Controversial Story" /> with around sixty episodes. It was during that planning phase that [[Stellan Skarsgård]], who plays Rael, joined the series, but he asked Gilroy to kill off his character at the end of season two so he did not have to stay for the entire series.<ref name="Vulture05-16-25">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/tony-gilroy-andor-star-wars-rogue-one-interview.html|text=‘Before Anyone Else Defines It, I’m Going to Define It’ Andor creator Tony Gilroy reflects on five years inside the Star Wars universe|author=VanArendonk, Kathryn|date=2025-05-16|work=''Vulture''|archivedate=20250519093736}}</ref> According to Gilroy, the five season ''Andor'' had the same overall story progression as the final series.<ref name="Controversial Story" /> In the end, he would decide to pivot to just two seasons and believes that he did not lose anything major.<ref name="Backstory05-17-25">{{YouTube|video=4EWCzic9z_M|text=Andor S2 Q&A - Tony Gilroy - Season Recap|channel=backstorymagazine2757|name=Backstory Magazine|date=2025-05-17}}</ref> Gilroy reflected that he had only planned out season one by the time he was heading into a writer's room.<ref name="Controversial Story" />

As recalled by Gilroy, the decision to shift to only two seasons came halfway through season one production as the scale of the production became clear to himself and the crew.<ref name="Radar03-26-25" /> Luna feared that he would visibly age over the production of five seasons.<ref name="Popverse, 2024-07-24">{{WebCite|url=https://www.thepopverse.com/tv-star-wars-andor-season-2-3-4-5-plans-changed-diego-luna-ace-2024|text=Star Wars: Andor star Diego Luna describes how they're fitting four seasons of planned story into the second (and final) season|author=apin-Bertone, Joshua|date=2024-07-24|work=''Pop Verse''|archivedate=20240803203145}}</ref> Furthermore, Gilroy believed that there was not enough story left in ''Andor'' for twelve episodes across four more seasons.<ref name="Screenrant11-21-24">{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-andor-five-season-story|text=Andor Was Originally Pitched As A Five-Season Story, So Why Are We Only Getting Two?|author=Bacon, Thomas|date=2024-11-21|archivedate=20250323194300}}</ref> As a solution, ''Andor'' was shortened to two seasons, with the second season featuring four story arcs that each covered a year of the timeline up to ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Popverse, 2024-07-24" /> In doing so, ''Andor'' fulfilled its purpose of telling a five year story. According to Gilroy, Luna and himself came to the decision together while drinking scotch.<ref name="Screenrant11-21-24" /> Luna, meanwhile, credits Gilroy for the "great idea."<ref name="Popverse, 2024-07-24" /> Gilroy considers season two "a fascinating experiment."<ref name="Radar03-26-25" />

===Production===
====Season one filming====
[[File:AndorSeries.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The original series logo revealed in 2020]]
On [[December 3]], 2020,<ref name="Kimmel Schedule">{{WebCite|url=https://abc.com/shows/jimmy-kimmel-live/news/schedule/jkl-schedule-for-11302020|text=Jimmy Kimmel Live Schedule for the Week of 11/30/2020|work=[[Wikipedia:American Broadcasting Company|ABC Entertainment]]|archivedate=20201204210812}}</ref> Diego Luna confirmed that the series had started filming in London.<ref name="Jimmy Kimmel">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@JimmyKimmelLive|name=Jimmy Kimmel Live|video=CjApD1utCIk|text=Diego Luna on Star Wars Spin-Off, His Father Hating Christmas & Recreating The Princess Bride}}</ref> The title of ''Andor'', as well as behind the scenes footage of the filming of the series, were unveiled on [[December 10]], 2020 at a [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] investors meeting. Filming began in late [[November]] of 2020.<ref name="Dec 10">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref><ref name="Sizzle">{{SWYouTube|gSW-pARyP-M|Sizzle Reel | Andor | Disney+|sw_url=video/sizzle-andor}}</ref> Although Alan Tudyk was initially announced to play K-2SO in the series,<ref name="D23">{{SW|url=news/the-galaxy-far-far-away-just-got-a-little-bigger|text=The Galaxy Far, Far Away Just Got A Little Bigger…}}</ref> he later clarified in [[January]] of [[2021]] that while production was underway, he was not going to appear in the first season. He did, however, expect to be brought into the fold in later seasons.<ref name="NoAlan">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/rogue-one-cassian-andor-series-cast-k2so-absence-explained-alan-tudyk-interview|text='Rogue One' Disney+ Series Won't Include K-2SO, Alan Tudyk Confirms — At Least At First|author=Drew Taylor|date=2021-01-20|archivedate=20210121012631}}</ref>

The showrunners opted for practical environments, with scenes being shot at [[Pinewood Studios]] and on location. One scene was shot at [[Wikipedia:Pitlochry|Pitlochry]], [[Wikipedia:Scotland|Scotland]],<ref name="Empire">{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/news/star-wars-andor-doesnt-use-volume-says-tony-gilroy-exclusive|text=Andor Doesn't Use Star Wars' Volume Video Wall: 'We're Old-School,' Says Tony Gilroy — Exclusive Image|author=Ben Travis|date=2022-01-08|archivedate=20220801153835}}</ref> while exterior scenes for the [[Aldhani dam]] were also filmed in Scotland, at the [[Wikipedia:Cruachan Power Station|Cruachan pumped storage hydro plant]].<ref name="Instagram-dam">{{Instagram|username=bencruachaninn|url=p/CiAmNIvK47K|name=Ben Cruachan Inn|date=2022-09-02|quote=Lots of excitement with the release of #starwars series #Andor}}</ref> [[Ferrix]] was very expensive to create. Gilroy stated its "mental build" took two years.<ref name="Perfect Episode">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/08/andor-secrets-awards-insider|text=''Andor'': Inside the Making of a Perfect Star Wars Episode|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2023-08-17|archivedate=20231024185917}}</ref> Filming wrapped in [[September]] 2021.<ref name="Diego Luna Andor Details">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2021/09/diego-luna-star-wars-andor-details-production-familiar-faces-1234845366|text=Diego Luna Says 'Star Wars: Andor' Has Finished Shooting, And To Expect "Familiar Faces"|author=Rosy Cordero|date=2021-09-27|archivedate=20210927235143}}</ref>

====Season two production====
=====Writers and Actors strikes=====
As part of the [[Wikipedia:2023 Writers Guild of America strike|2023 Writers Guild of America strike]], Gilroy ceased all services on ''Andor'' and did not return to the set.<ref name="Gilroy Ceases">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/andor-tony-gilroy-scabbing-accusations-strike-1235483978|text=Showrunner Tony Gilroy Ceases Producing Services on ‘Andor’ (Exclusive)|date=2023-05-09|archivedate=20230730022000}}</ref> A few weeks before season two's UK shoot was to finish, ''[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|Deadline Hollywood]]'' opened an article by stating that filming on season two would pause as a result of the [[Wikipedia:2023 SAG-AFTRA strike|2023 SAG-AFTRA actors strike]]. Later in the piece, however, the article stated that, as per what ''Deadline'' had learned, the series was still being filmed at Pinewood Studios, but without actors who were part of SAG-AFTRA: American SAG-AFTRA actors had stopped work, as per the strike, while members of the [[Wikipedia:Equity (British trade union)|British Equity union]] remained. According to the report, actors who were part of Equity were warned of potential legal action should they stop work in solidarity with the American union.<ref name="Filming cuts short">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2023/07/andor-star-wars-disney-cut-short-sag-aftra-strike-1235442836|text=‘Andor’ Season 2 Shoot To Be Cut Short Amid SAG-AFTRA Strike|date=2023-07-20|archivedate=20230731151037}}</ref>

=====Post-strikes=====
{{Quote|That's been our attitude all the way through: not to be cynical, and to take it more seriously than anybody ever took it. Even while we’re changing—some people feel as though it's changing a lot—but even while we're changing the grammar of what you can do, we’re trying very rigorously to be more serious about this shit than anybody ever has been.|Tony Gilroy, on making ''Andor''|<ref name="Gilroy Gizmodo">{{WebCite|url=https://gizmodo.com/star-wars-tony-gilroy-andor-interview-season-2-2000573377|text=Tony Gilroy Looks Back on Taking Shit Seriously in Andor|archivedate=20250320172737}}</ref>}}

It was already in pre-production by [[May]] [[2022]] and started production on [[November 21]], 2022;{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-season-2-filming|text=Here's When 'Andor' Season 2 Starts Filming [Exclusive]|date=2022-11-04|archivedate=20221104211108}} it was set for release in [[2024]],{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-season-2-timeline-explained|text=Tony Gilroy Reveals When 'Andor' Season 2 Begins|author=Maggie Lovitt|date=2022-11-23|archivedate=20241209162943}} but was later confirmed to release in [[2025]] starting on [[April 22]], 2025. While [[Andor Season 1|Season 1]] took place entirely in [[5 BBY]], Season 2 takes place over the course of four [[Standard year|year]]s. Separated into four three-episode blocks, each showing a few days of a year, the final block leads into the [[Mission to the Ring of Kafrene|opening scene]] of the film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'',{{WebCite|url=https://www.fandom.com/articles/andor-finale-season-1-spoilers-2|text=‘Andor’ Creator Talks Season 1 Finale Spoilers and Where Season 2 Will Go|author=Eric Goldman|date=2022-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Fandom (website)|Fandom.com]] {{C|Articles}}|archivedate=20241009160311}}{{BookCite|author=Ryan, Mike|container=Andor Season 2|title=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|number=January 2025|publisher=[[Wikipedia:Bauer Media Group|Bauer Media Group]]|date=2024-11-21|pages=pp. 49-53}} which is set in [[1 BBY]]. ==Official synopsis== ''Cassian Andor continues the path toward his heroic rebel destiny.'' ==Official description== ''Lucasfilm’s Emmy®-winning thriller “Andor,” returns for its long-awaited conclusion [on April 23]. The second season takes place as the horizon of war draws near and Cassian becomes a key player in the Rebel Alliance. Everyone will be tested and, as the stakes rise, the betrayals, sacrifices and conflicting agendas will become profound. Rife with political intrigue and danger, the series is a prequel to “Rogue One: A Star Wars Story,” which portrayed a heroic band of rebels who steal the plans to the Empire’s weapon of mass destruction—The Death Star—setting the stage for the events of the original 1977 film. “Andor” sets the clock back five years from the events of “Rogue One” to tell the story of the film’s hero, Cassian Andor, and his transformation from disinterested, cynical nobody into a rebel hero on his way to an epic destiny.''{{Disney|subdomain=press|domain=co.uk|url=press-kit/andor-season-2-press-kit|text=Andor Season Two Press Kit}} ==Official alternative description== ''Rife with political intrigue, danger, tension, and high stakes, “Andor” is a prequel to “Rogue One: A Star Wars Story", which portrayed a heroic band of rebels who steal the plans to the Empire’s weapon of mass destruction: The Death Star, setting the stage for the events of the original 1977 film. “Andor” sets the clock back five years from the events of “Rogue One” to tell the story of the film’s hero, Cassian Andor, and his transformation from disinterested, cynical nobody into a rebel hero on his way to an epic destiny.'' ''Andor Season 2 will see the characters and their relationships intensify as the horizon of war draws near and Cassian becomes a key player in the Rebel Alliance. Everyone will be tested and, as the stakes rise, the betrayals, sacrifices and conflicting agendas will become profound.'' ==Development== [[File:AndorS2Pitch-AndorZine.png|thumb|left|200px|The pitch for ''Andor'' Season Two dated to December of 2022]] {{Quote|No one goes in a revolution if it's not for love, for a real need of bringing change for a community. ''[…]'' It's a love story. There's no revolution without love.|Diego Luna, on ''Andor''|{{YouTube|channel=heyuguysblog|name=HeyUGuys|video=a_KQmQpalgY|text=Andor Season 2 - Revolution Needs Passion: Love Fuels Change|date=2025-04-11}}}} According to writer [[Tony Gilroy]], the plot of ''Andor'' was based on historical revolutions.{{WebCite|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/0/tony-gilroy-interview-andor-star-wars-disney-plus|text=Andor creator Tony Gilroy: ‘My Star Wars characters are based more on Trotsky than Trump’|author=Stephen Armstrong|date=2025-04-23|archivedate=20250423093955}} [[Diego Luna]], who played Cassian Andor, said in an interview in [[April 11]], 2025 that revolutions are based on love. [[Elizabeth Dulau]], who played Kleya Marki, said in an interview published on [[April 28]] that beneath the rigid veneer of her character was "a lot of love" that motivated her to sacrifice her daily life for the rebellion.{{WebCite|url=https://vogue.sg/elizabeth-dulau-kleya-marki-andor-season-2|text=“The rebellion is her entire life”: Elizabeth Dulau on playing Kleya Marki in ‘Andor’ Season 2|author=Azrin Tan|date=2025-04-28|work=[[Wikipedia:Vogue Singapore|''Vogue Singapore'']]|archivedate=20250428122249}} Gilroy said that he used historical revolutions as a catalog for fictional stories, with a focus on exploring the behavioral aspect of individuals—such as what they fear or the banal selfishness of agents of the state—and integrating them with the journey of a character like Cassian Andor waking up to political consciousness. Among the early work he did for ''Andor'' was figuring out what ideal futures would characters have in mind following their revolution, but Gilroy deliberately left any discussion of the future out of Season 2 because the characters would be too busy fighting the Empire.{{YouTube|video=SUUw-UfK64Q|text=Andor, Trump and Our Revolutionary Times|channel=@WeeklyShowPodcast|name=The Weekly Show with Jon Stewart|date=2025-07-10}} According to Gilroy, a litany of historical events therefore informed his story in ''Andor'', such as the Soviet revolutionaries [[Wikipedia:Leon Trotsky|Leon Trotsky]] and [[Wikipedia:Joseph Stalin|Joseph Stalin]] who [[Wikipedia:1907 Tiflis bank robbery|robbed a bank]] to fund the revolution, or the French Resistance comprising [[Wikipedia:Charles de Gaulle|Gaullists]], Communists, and the [[Wikipedia:Maquis (World War II)|Maquis]] who hated each other. A part of ''Andor'' Season 2 was filmed at the [[Wikipedia:City of Arts and Sciences|City of Arts and Sciences]] complex in [[Wikipedia:Valencia|Valencia]].{{WebCite|url=https://vogue.sg/elizabeth-dulau-kleya-marki-andor-season-2|text=“The rebellion is her entire life”: Elizabeth Dulau on playing Kleya Marki in ‘Andor’ Season 2|author=Azrin Tan|date=2025-04-28|work=[[Wikipedia:Vogue Singapore|''Vogue Singapore'']]|archivedate=20250428122249}} According to [[Michael Wilkinson]], around 4,045 costumes were created for the second season.{{Instagram|username=michaelwilkinson|url=stories/michaelwilkinson/3683246582855845882|name=Michael Wilkinson|date=2025-07-24|quote=At a rough count, for Season 2, we made about 3,050 costumes for Extras, 715 costumes for Principal Cast, 115 costumes for Creatures and about 165 costumes for Stunts – so all in all, about 4,045 costumes! We had 4 workrooms in-house at Pinewood studios in London – Men’s cast, Women’s cast, Secondary cast and Crowd – and then we also had outside workrooms making costumes for us when we ran out of room! For Andor Season 1, we made over 3,000 costumes.|nolive=1}} ==Release and reception== Season 2's trailer, released in February 2025, uses [[Wikipedia:Steve Earle|Steve Earle's]] [[2004]] [[Wikipedia:Cowpunk|country punk]] song [[Wikipedia:The Revolution Starts Now (album)|''The Revolution Starts Now'']],{{SWYouTube|AE4wxt70aUM|Andor | Season 2 Trailer | Streaming April 22 on Disney+}} which addresses how citizens ought to actively defend American [[democracy]] in light of the [[Wikipedia:2004 United States elections|election]] and ongoing [[Wikipedia:Iraq War|war in Iraq]] that year.Liner notes of [[Wikipedia:The Revolution Starts Now (album)|''The Revolution Starts Now'']] — {{WebCite|url=https://www.steveearle.net/discography/revolution.php|text=The Revolution Starts…Now|work=[https://www.steveearle.net SteveEarle.net]|archivedate=20241201170414}} In an interview with [[Wikipedia:The Daily Telegraph|''The Telegraph'']] published on [[April 23]], 2025, Tony Gilroy was asked if there was any order from Lucasfilm to "adjust the depiction of the Empire in light of a presidency that could be seen to mirror it" in light of Donald Trump's [[Wikipedia:Second presidency of Donald Trump|second term]] as US President. Gilroy replied that he would be asking the same question if he was in the interviewer's place but elaborated that his story and characters were based on historical revolutions. In an interview conducted ahead of Season 2's premiere and published on [[May 13]], [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] asked Gilroy about motifs of unrest across ''Andor'', noting how the series "summons images of [[Wikipedia:Russo-Ukrainian War|Ukraine]], [[Wikipedia:Gaza war|Gaza]], [[Wikipedia:Fall of Kabul (2021)|Kabul]] and [[Wikipedia:2019–2020 Hong Kong protests|Hong Kong]]" of current affairs "alongside references to the French Revolution, [[Wikipedia:Oliver Cromwell|Oliver Cromwell]] and Nazi propaganda" in past history—Gilroy said that he was writing about all revolutions and insurrections and how he felt that people, including himself, often have a narcissistic and individualistic belief that they are living in a unique time of history despite that not being "the pattern of history." Nevertheless, seeing audiences draw current real-world parallels to the series, such as a sense of authoritarianism threatening democracies like the United States, is a reflection on "if people find history knocking at their door, there's probably all kinds of places they can look for references."{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/andor-finale-diego-luna-tony-gilroy-star-wars-1236394652|text=Andor Finale: Diego Luna, Tony Gilroy on Revolutionizing 'Star Wars'|author=Adam B. Vary|date=2025-05-13|archivedate=20250513161511}} On the same day, Gilroy said during a livestream on the official ''Star Wars'' YouTube channel that fascism not only destroys the people that the ideology is used to target but also the people who enact it, referring to [[Dedra Meero]] and [[Syril Karn]].{{SWYouTube|uvkpcedAtXs|Andor Season 2 with Diego Luna and Tony Gilroy LIVE | Now Streaming on Disney+}} Dedra Meero's actor, [[Denise Gough]], expressed in interviews her belief that artists like herself using their platforms to speak up for the Palestinian people is important to keep up a groundswell of support through democracies like Ireland for the rights of other people.{{YouTube|video=_omQdodjg_M|text=‘Andor’ Star: I Refuse to Stay Silent on Gaza|channel=@BreakThroughNews|name=BreakThrough News|date=2025-05-31}} When asked about including the word "genocide" in a ''Star Wars'' series at the ATX TV Festival of [[May 29]]–[[June 1]], Gilroy expressed that it is sad that many people could find an immediate emotional resonance with the word; ''Andor'' writer [[Beau Willimon]] mentioned he also found that people could find the series motivating for their own actions, with Gilroy adding to the cheers of the audience that Willimon himself has made personal sacrifices as president of the [[Wikipedia:Writers Guild of America, East|Writers Guild of America, East]].{{YouTube|video=FMOw6gP4r7Q|text=ANDOR with Tony Gilroy & Beau Willimon | ATX TV Festival|channel=@ATXTV|name=ATX TV|date=2025-06-10}} In [[Wikipedia:Ross Douthat|Ross Douthat's]] interview of Gilroy for [[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']] that was published on [[June 5]], the two discussed how ''Andor'' focused on the destruction of community and the future of AI. Gilroy said he had discussed AI with people in [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles|Los Angeles]] in the past few days and came across the "terrifying" prospect of a [[Wikipedia:AI alignment|misaligned]] AI superintelligence killing all humans arriving as early as [[2027]], or alternative dystopic scenarios such as mass unemployment and an AI nuclear race between the United States and China.{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/05/opinion/film-hollywood-andor-politics.html|text=What Makes Art ‘Left Wing’?|author=[[Wikipedia:Ross Douthat|Ross Douthat]]|date=2025-06-05|archivedate=20250606092427}} In a podcast recorded with the host [[Wikipedia:Jon Stewart|Jon Stewart]] and historian [[Wikipedia:Mike Duncan (podcaster)|Mike Duncan]] on [[July 9]], Gilroy discussed his use of historical revolutions and how he realized overcoming a common obstacle like the Galactic Empire or the Russian tsarist regime took precedent for the people directly involved, ahead of any discussion on a desired future after the fight and without a common goal. Duncan agreed and added that a common feature of revolutions is that they start with ideals and slogans such as freedom and democracy but spiral out of any individual's control, and once they had successfully removed a regime, authority, sovereignty, and legitimacy had to be [[Wikipedia:Constructivism (international relations)|reconstructed]] and inevitably lead to the movement's splintering, allowing the influence of power-seeking figures such as Lenin to dominate. In the same vein, Gilroy said he had adapted the "authoritarian playbook" of "building the enemy you want," giving the examples of [[Wikipedia:J. Edgar Hoover|J. Edgar Hoover]] with the civil rights and anti-war movements, the British state with the [[Wikipedia:Provisional Irish Republican Army|IRA]], or [[Wikipedia:Benjamin Netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] with [[Wikipedia:Hamas|Hamas]], complementing the spontaneous nature of uprisings, such as the [[Wikipedia:Tunisian revolution|martyr]] of the Arab Spring. The podcasters then discussed the US seemingly becoming a "tinderbox." Gilroy had thought about some of the audiences' remarks that ''Andor'' has been "predictive" of America in the past six months, with the mineral rights over Ghorman echoing the US' ambitions over [[Wikipedia:Greenland|Greenland]], the migrantion issue on [[Mina-Rau]] echoing the US [[Wikipedia:United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)]] agency's [[Wikipedia:Deportation in the second presidency of Donald Trump|hardline deportation operations]], and the [[Arrest of Dasi Oran|arrest]] of Senator Dasi Oran in the Senate Building echoing US Senator [[Wikipedia:Alex Padilla|Alex Padilla]] being forcibly detained at a federal press conference. Gilroy added he was surprised a confrontation over an ICE raid had not yet led to an event akin to the [[Wikipedia:Kent State shootings|Kent State shootings]] during the anti-war protests in 1970 and prompted a declaration of martial law, and he suggested a civil conflict would then perhaps be a desired outcome for the "tech right" like [[Wikipedia:Peter Thiel|Peter Thiel]] of [[Wikipedia:Palantir Technologies|Palantir Technologies]] who are using Trump as a "host organism" and, as expressed in the interview with Ross Douthat on [[June 26]], would not care if AI wipes out humanity. Gilroy recalled that the fantasy author [[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien]] disliked allegories and pointed out that they are different from applicability—Gilroy realized that the audience of ''Andor'' have found the story applicable to many different contexts. Although he was hesitant, especially at the start of Season 2's press tour, to let interviewers associate political labels with ''Andor'', he has felt sadness as people around the world find ''Andor'' resonating deeply with their own experiences. The podcast speakers nevertheless expressed hope that the series, having become part of contemporary popular culture, could help people adapt to the changing times. ==Media== {{Mediacat|from=1|imagecat=Images from Andor Season 2}} ===Episodes=== {| {{Prettytable}} !
